facts.text: Seismometer was deployed at Chryse Planitia during Viking 1 in 1976.

The seismometer on Viking 1 was mounted on top of the lander, which meant it was sensitive to wind vibrations. Unlike its twin on Viking 2, which may have detected a marsquake, Viking 1's seismometer was unable to confirm any seismic events due to wind interference. The lesson informed the design of InSight's seismometer decades later.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Attempted the first seismic measurements on Mars; its wind-interference problems taught engineers to place future seismometers directly on the ground.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Chryse Planitia.
Its failure directly inspired the design of InSight's SEIS seismometer, which was placed on the surface and successfully detected over 1,300 marsquakes.
